title: X x_{Spec A} Spec(A/K) -> X is the closed immersion cut out by K O_X
statement: Let $A$ be a ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $f:X\to S$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. For an ideal $K\subseteq A$ let $X_K=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}(A/K)$ be the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] with first projection $j_K:X_K\to X$, regard $X_K$ as a scheme over $S$ through $f\circ j_K$, and let $K\mathcal O_X\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be the image of $f^*\widetilde K\to f^*\mathcal O_S\to\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] ($\widetilde K\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ the ideal sheaf associated to $K$), and likewise $K\mathcal O_{X_K}$ for $X_K\to S$. (1) $j_K$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] is $K\mathcal O_X$; for every affine open $U\subseteq X$, with $B=\mathcal O_X(U)$ (an $A$-algebra via $f$), $j_K^{-1}(U)$ is affine, $j_K^{-1}(U)\to U$ is identified over $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B/KB)\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ induced by the quotient map, and $(K\mathcal O_X)(U)=KB$. (2) For ideals $K,K'\subseteq A$, $(K\mathcal O_X)\cdot(K'\mathcal O_X)=(KK')\mathcal O_X$ (product of quasi-coherent ideal sheaves [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]); in particular $(K\mathcal O_X)^m=K^m\mathcal O_X$ for $m\ge1$. (3) Let $J\subseteq J'$ be ideals of $A$. The morphism $i:X_{J'}\to X_J$ with $j_J\circ i=j_{J'}$ whose composite with the second projection $X_J\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ is $X_{J'}\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/J')\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ (it exists and is unique by the universal property of $X_J$) is a closed immersion with ideal sheaf $J'\mathcal O_{X_J}$; over an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $X$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J'B)\to\operatorname{Spec}(B/JB)$, induced by the quotient map. (4) For every ideal $L\subseteq A$, the image of $j_K^*(L\mathcal O_X)\to j_K^*\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_{X_K}$ (the ideal $(L\mathcal O_X)\mathcal O_{X_K}$ of [def-nagata-extended-ideal] for $j_K$) equals $L\mathcal O_{X_K}$; over $j_K^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}(B/KB)$ both are $L\cdot(B/KB)$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01JU (lemma-fibre-product-immersion) part (1): the base change of the closed immersion Spec(A/K) -> Spec A along f is the closed subscheme cut out by Im(f^* K~ -> O_X); Lemmas 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes) and 01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affines) for the affine description Spec(B (x)_A A/K) = Spec(B/KB); Lemma 01IN (lemma-closed-subspace-scheme) for the ideal on affine opens; the use with K = I^{n+1} is Cohomology of Schemes, Remark 088F (remark-reformulate-existence-theorem), literature/stacks-project/coherent.tex, which leaves it implicit (statement assembled by the agent)

proof.text: (Notation, the ideal $\widetilde K$, and equality on a basis.) Write $c_K:\operatorname{Spec}(A/K)\to S$ for $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the quotient map $A\to A/K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $p_K:X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/K)$ for the second projection, so $f\circ j_K=c_K\circ p_K$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For an affine open $U\subseteq X$ with $B=\mathcal O_X(U)$ let $\rho_U:A=\mathcal O_S(S)\to B$ be $f^\sharp_S$ followed by restriction to $U$; under the canonical $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ the morphism $f|_U:U\to S$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\rho_U$ (a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of exactly one ring map, its map on global sections [def-weil-affine-spectrum]), and $KB$ means $\rho_U(K)B$. The ideal sheaf $\widetilde K\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ is quasi-coherent and $\widetilde K(S)=K$: by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] $\widetilde K$ is quasi-coherent with $\widetilde K(D(r))=K_r$, the inclusion $K\subseteq A$ induces $\widetilde K\to\widetilde A=\mathcal O_S$, injective on every $D(r)$ since $K_r\to A_r$ is injective (localization is exact), and for $r=1$, $D(1)=S$ and $\tau_S:K\to\widetilde K(S)$ is a localization at the powers of $1$, i.e. an isomorphism onto $K\subseteq A$. Hence by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] (1), applied to $f:X\to Y=S$, $\mathcal J=\widetilde K$ and $V=S$: $K\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal O_X$ and $(K\mathcal O_X)(U)=\rho_U(K)B=KB$ for every affine open $U\subseteq X$; the same holds for every ideal of $A$ and every scheme over $S$ (in particular for $X_K$ over $S$ via $f\circ j_K$), and, with $A/J$ in place of $A$, for schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$. Finally, two sub-$\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal S,\mathcal S'$ of a sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a scheme with $\mathcal S(U)=\mathcal S'(U)$ for all $U$ in a basis $\mathfrak B$ of the topology are equal: for $s\in\mathcal S(W)$ cover $W$ by members $U_k$ of $\mathfrak B$; the $s|_{U_k}\in\mathcal S'(U_k)$ agree on overlaps and glue in the sheaf $\mathcal S'$ to $t\in\mathcal S'(W)$, and $t=s$ in $\mathcal F$; symmetrically. The affine opens of a scheme form a basis [def-pc-scheme].

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01IN (lemma-closed-subspace-scheme) for quasi-coherent ideals on affine opens; written by the agent

proof.text: ($j_K$ is a closed immersion.) $c_K$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] (2) applied to the one-member affine cover $\{S\}$ of $S$: $c_K^{-1}(S)=\operatorname{Spec}(A/K)$ is affine and $(c_K)^\sharp_S:A\to A/K$ is the quotient map (the map on global sections of $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a ring map is that ring map [def-weil-affine-spectrum]), which is surjective. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] with $i=c_K$ and $g=f$, the projection $\operatorname{Spec}(A/K)\times_SX\to X$ is a closed immersion. Exchanging the factors, $(X_K,p_K,j_K)$ is a fibre product of $c_K$ and $f$ with first projection to $\operatorname{Spec}(A/K)$, so by uniqueness of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] there is an isomorphism $\theta:X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/K)\times_SX$ with $j_K$ equal to the projection to $X$ composed with $\theta$. A closed immersion composed with an isomorphism on the source is a closed immersion (the image and the map $\mathcal O_X\to j_{K*}\mathcal O_{X_K}$ are unchanged up to the isomorphism $\theta_*$), so $j_K$ is a closed immersion.

proof.text: (Affine description of $j_K$ over $U$.) Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open, $B=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $\iota_U:U\to X$ the inclusion. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] applied to $j_K$ and the open $U$, the square with corners $j_K^{-1}(U)\to U$ (restriction of $j_K$), $j_K^{-1}(U)\to X_K$ (inclusion), $U\to X$, $X_K\to X$ is cartesian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] to the diagram whose upper square is this one and whose lower square is the cartesian square of $X_K$ ($j_K:X_K\to X$ over $c_K:\operatorname{Spec}(A/K)\to S$, with vertical maps $p_K$ and $f$): the upper square is cartesian, so the outer rectangle is, i.e. $j_K^{-1}(U)$ with the maps $j_K|:j_K^{-1}(U)\to U$ and $p_K|:j_K^{-1}(U)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/K)$ is a fibre product of $f\circ\iota_U=\operatorname{Spec}\rho_U$ (step 1) and $c_K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] (with $R=A$, the $A$-algebras $B$ via $\rho_U$ and $A/K$), $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_AA/K)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $b\mapsto b\otimes1$ and $\bar a\mapsto1\otimes\bar a$ is also such a fibre product, so by uniqueness [def-pc-fibre-product] $j_K^{-1}(U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_AA/K)$ compatibly with the maps to $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change], $B/KB\to B\otimes_AA/K$, $\bar b\mapsto b\otimes1$, is an isomorphism of $B$-algebras, so composing with $\operatorname{Spec}$ of it: $j_K^{-1}(U)$ is affine and $j_K^{-1}(U)\to U$ is identified over $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the quotient map $B\to B/KB$. In particular the ring map $(j_K)^\sharp_U:B\to\mathcal O_{X_K}(j_K^{-1}U)$ is identified with $B\to B/KB$, and the composite $A\to B\to B/KB$ is the ring map of $(f\circ j_K)|_{j_K^{-1}(U)}$ on global sections.

(Clause (1): the ideal sheaf.) Let $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to j_{K*}\mathcal O_{X_K})$ be the ideal sheaf of the closed immersion $j_K$ (step 2) [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]; it is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, and on an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, where $j_K^{-1}(U)\to U$ is identified with $\operatorname{Spec}(B/KB)\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ (step 3), $\mathcal I(U)=KB$. By step 1, $(K\mathcal O_X)(U)=KB$ as well. So the sub-$\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal I$ and $K\mathcal O_X$ of $\mathcal O_X$ agree on the basis of affine opens, and are equal by step 1. With step 3 this is (1).

proof.text: (Clause (2).) $K\mathcal O_X$, $K'\mathcal O_X$ and $(KK')\mathcal O_X$ are quasi-coherent ideals with sections $KB$, $K'B$, $(KK')B$ on an affine open $U$ with ring $B$ (step 1). Their product $(K\mathcal O_X)(K'\mathcal O_X)$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers] is the quasi-coherent ideal with sections $(KB)(K'B)$ on $U$. Now $(KB)(K'B)=(KK')B$: the left side is generated as an ideal by the products $\rho_U(k)\rho_U(k')=\rho_U(kk')$, $k\in K$, $k'\in K'$, and $KK'$ is additively generated by the $kk'$, so both ideals have the same generators. Hence the two ideals agree on all affine opens and are equal (step 1). The powers follow by induction on $m$: $(K\mathcal O_X)^1=K\mathcal O_X$, and $(K\mathcal O_X)^{m+1}=(K\mathcal O_X)^m(K\mathcal O_X)=(K^m\mathcal O_X)(K\mathcal O_X)=(K^{m+1})\mathcal O_X$ by the product formula with $K^m$ and $K$ in place of $K,K'$.

proof.text: (Clause (3): the morphism $i$ and a cartesian square.) Let $c_{J',J}:\operatorname{Spec}(A/J')\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ be $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the quotient map $A/J\to A/J'$; then $c_J\circ c_{J',J}=c_{J'}$ by functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], as $A\to A/J\to A/J'$ is the quotient map. Since $f\circ j_{J'}=c_{J'}\circ p_{J'}=c_J\circ(c_{J',J}\circ p_{J'})$, the universal property of $X_J$ [def-pc-fibre-product] gives exactly one $i:X_{J'}\to X_J$ with $j_J\circ i=j_{J'}$ and $p_J\circ i=c_{J',J}\circ p_{J'}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] to the diagram with left column $X_{J'}\xrightarrow{i}X_J\xrightarrow{j_J}X$, right column $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J')\xrightarrow{c_{J',J}}\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)\xrightarrow{c_J}S$ and horizontal maps $p_{J'},p_J,f$: both squares commute, the lower square is the cartesian square of $X_J$, and the outer rectangle ($X_{J'}$ with $p_{J'}$ and $j_J\circ i=j_{J'}$, over $c_J\circ c_{J',J}=c_{J'}$ and $f$) is the cartesian square of $X_{J'}$; hence the upper square is cartesian: $(X_{J'},i,p_{J'})$ is a fibre product of $p_J:X_J\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ and $c_{J',J}$.

proof.text: (Clause (3): closed immersion, ideal sheaf, affine description.) Put $\bar A=A/J$ and $\bar J'=J'/J\subseteq\bar A$. The isomorphism $\bar A/\bar J'\cong A/J'$ compatible with the quotient maps from $\bar A$ makes $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J')\to\operatorname{Spec}\bar A$ isomorphic over $\operatorname{Spec}\bar A$ to $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $\bar A\to\bar A/\bar J'$, so by step 6 and uniqueness of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] there is an isomorphism $\psi:X_{J'}\to(X_J)_{\bar J'}:=X_J\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\bar A}\operatorname{Spec}(\bar A/\bar J')$ with $i$ equal to the first projection composed with $\psi$. Steps 2-4 applied to $p_J:X_J\to\operatorname{Spec}\bar A$ and the ideal $\bar J'$ show that this first projection is a closed immersion with ideal sheaf $\bar J'\mathcal O_{X_J}$ (formed for $p_J$), hence so is $i$ (composition with an isomorphism changes neither the image nor $\ker(\mathcal O_{X_J}\to i_*\mathcal O_{X_{J'}})$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]). Moreover $\bar J'\mathcal O_{X_J}=J'\mathcal O_{X_J}$ (the latter formed for $f\circ j_J=c_J\circ p_J$): for an affine open $W\subseteq X_J$ with ring $C$, step 1 gives $(J'\mathcal O_{X_J})(W)$ = the ideal generated by the image of $J'$ under $A\to\bar A\to C$ (the global-sections map of $c_J\circ p_J|_W$ is the composite) and $(\bar J'\mathcal O_{X_J})(W)$ = the ideal generated by the image of $\bar J'$ under $\bar A\to C$; as $\bar J'$ is the image of $J'$ in $\bar A$ these have the same generators, so the two ideals agree on all affine opens and are equal (step 1). Over an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $X$: $W=j_J^{-1}(U)$ is affine with ring $B/JB$ (step 3 for $J$), $i^{-1}(W)=j_{J'}^{-1}(U)$, and step 3 for $p_J$ and $\bar J'$ identifies $i^{-1}(W)\to W$ with $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the quotient map $B/JB\to(B/JB)/\bar J'(B/JB)$; here $\bar J'(B/JB)=(J'B+JB)/JB=J'B/JB$ as $J\subseteq J'$, and $(B/JB)/(J'B/JB)=B/J'B$, so $i$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J'B)\to\operatorname{Spec}(B/JB)$ induced by the quotient map.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01JU (1) applied over Spec(A/J); written by the agent

proof.text: (Clause (4).) Let $L\subseteq A$ be an ideal. By step 1, $L\mathcal O_X$ is a quasi-coherent ideal of $\mathcal O_X$ with $(L\mathcal O_X)(U)=LB$ on affine opens $U$ with ring $B$, and the ideal sheaf of $j_K$ has $\mathcal I(U)=KB$ (step 4). By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-ideal-powers] (1) for the closed immersion $j_K$ and the quasi-coherent ideal $L\mathcal O_X$, $(L\mathcal O_X)\mathcal O_{X_K}$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] is a quasi-coherent ideal of $\mathcal O_{X_K}$ with sections $LB\cdot(B/KB)=L\cdot(B/KB)$ on $j_K^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}(B/KB)$. By step 1 for $X_K$ over $S$, $L\mathcal O_{X_K}$ is a quasi-coherent ideal with sections on the affine open $j_K^{-1}(U)$ the ideal generated by the image of $L$ under $A\to B\to B/KB$ (step 3), i.e. $L\cdot(B/KB)$. The opens $j_K^{-1}(U)$, $U\subseteq X$ affine, form a basis of $X_K$: $j_K$ is a homeomorphism onto its image [def-weil-closed-immersion], so an open $W'\ni z$ of $X_K$ is $j_K^{-1}(O)$ for an open $O\subseteq X$, and an affine open $U$ with $j_K(z)\in U\subseteq O$ gives $z\in j_K^{-1}(U)\subseteq W'$. So the two ideals agree on a basis and are equal (step 1).
